question_bank.stem: A benchmark dashboard shows one checkpoint doing poorly on reasoning. What diagnostic use of benchmarks does this illustrate?

options.text: Finding capability-specific error clusters across checkpoints
Computing pixel gradients for the reasoning class
Increasing the spatial size of a generator output
Selecting a max-pooling switch for reconstruction

question_bank.rationale: The lecture says benchmarks across tasks can reveal error clusters, such as a checkpoint doing poorly at reasoning.

distractor_rationales.B: Pixel gradients are a CNN saliency method.
distractor_rationales.C: Generator output size relates to deconvolution.
distractor_rationales.D: Pooling switches are used in DeconvNet visualizations.

frame_evidence.description: Slide shows capability benchmark dashboards across reasoning, coding, math, and multilingual tasks.

question_bank.stem: A public math benchmark appears in training blogs and GitHub files. What risk does the lecture associate with this situation?

options.text: The benchmark test set may be contaminated by training data
The loss curve must be smooth by construction
The class activation map must be retrained
The MoE router must balance experts perfectly

question_bank.rationale: The instructor warns that public benchmark material can appear online and contaminate training data.

distractor_rationales.B: Training-data exposure does not guarantee smooth loss curves.
distractor_rationales.C: CAM retraining is unrelated to benchmark exposure.
distractor_rationales.D: MoE router balance is a separate training diagnostic.

source_ref.evidence_span: All of those might contaminate benchmarks.

frame_evidence.description: Slide shows benchmark-contamination checks using train/test comparisons such as n-grams, hashes, and embeddings.

question_bank.stem: To test whether benchmark examples leaked into training data, which detection methods does the lecture list?

options.text: N-gram search, hashes, and embedding-based semantic search
Global average pooling, class weights, and saliency maps
Unpooling switches, flipped filters, and fractional stride
Learning-rate warmup, RLHF rewards, and PPO clipping

question_bank.rationale: The contamination section names n-grams, hashes, and embeddings as ways to find exact or semantic overlap between training and test data.

distractor_rationales.B: These are CNN attribution/CAM components, not contamination checks.
distractor_rationales.C: These are DeconvNet or transposed-convolution components.
distractor_rationales.D: These are training or RLHF ideas, not the listed contamination-detection methods.

source_ref.evidence_span: You can do it also with hashes or with embeddings.

frame_evidence.description: Slide shows benchmark-contamination checks using train/test comparisons such as n-grams, hashes, and embeddings.

question_bank.stem: When exposed benchmark items are found, what repair does the lecture recommend for the test set?

options.text: Remove the exposed examples and replace them with newly held-out ones
Keep the exposed examples and average them with training loss
Convert the exposed examples into softmax probabilities
Route the exposed examples to a single MoE expert

question_bank.rationale: The instructor says to fix the test set by removing exposed examples and replacing them with brand-new held-out examples.

distractor_rationales.B: Keeping exposed examples would preserve the contamination problem.
distractor_rationales.C: Softmax probabilities do not repair a contaminated benchmark.
distractor_rationales.D: Expert routing is unrelated to benchmark repair.

source_ref.evidence_span: You would remove all those examples

question_bank.stem: Safety dashboards for foundation models should include agentic-workflow tests because they evaluate what extra behavior beyond one-shot answers?

options.text: How the model behaves while using tools across a workflow
How a dog-class score changes under a dark square
How a deconvolution matrix inserts zeros
How an image generator increases spatial size

question_bank.rationale: The lecture says safety evaluation should include how the model behaves in an agentic workflow, not only one-shot evaluation.

distractor_rationales.B: That describes occlusion sensitivity, not safety evaluation.

source_ref.evidence_span: model behaves in an agentic workflow,
